title: Renfe starts notifying customers of a September data breach
date_note: Date of Renfe's individual notices to travellers as reported by Público and elDiario.es; Renfe dates the unauthorised access to 24 September 2026. Público says Renfe made the incident public on 28 September; elDiario.es says Renfe acknowledged the intrusion on 25 September.
geo_basis: country as stated; Madrid used as the national point
summary: Renfe says a third party gained unauthorised access to some of its systems on 24 September 2026. Público reports its customer notices say the data involved includes contact details, DNI or NIE numbers, ticket and travel history, and encrypted passwords. Renfe says it has no evidence of fraudulent use. Público says a suspect was detained in October; elDiario.es could not verify that and says Renfe gave no customer count.
plain: Spain's rail operator Renfe is writing to travellers about a September breach that, it says, involved names, contact details, ID numbers, ticket history and encrypted passwords.
exec: A national rail operator's customer data, including ID document numbers, is involved; phishing and impersonation risk for travellers.
action: If you have a Renfe account, change its password and any reused one; do not share passwords or codes by email, SMS or phone; questions to dpdviajeros@renfe.es.
impact: Customer personal data involved; the notice as reported gives no number of people.

validation.note: Público and elDiario.es (both 20 Nov 2026) independently report Renfe's customer notice: data involved, 24 September access, advice to change passwords. elDiario.es says it could not verify the arrest.

review.note: Compared with Publico and elDiario (20 Nov): data types, 24 Sept access, no-fraud statement, arrest, notices match; date_note said disclosure 28 Sept but elDiario says 25 Sept, now both stated; correction filed
